findings.issue: The admission agreement form that the buyer must use for 12 months after closing requires the resident to sign the arbitration agreement as a condition of admission and allows rescission for only three days. A facility may not make arbitration a condition of admission and must allow rescission within 30 calendar days of signing.
findings.quote: Resident agrees, as a condition of admission to the Facility, to sign the Resident-Facility Arbitration Agreement attached as Attachment 4. Resident may rescind the Arbitration Agreement by written notice delivered to the Administrator within three (3) days after signing.

findings.issue: The closing is fixed for the 45th day after signing regardless of Department approval, and the change of ownership application is filed only within 15 business days after signing. No one may acquire or operate a skilled nursing facility before the Department approves and issues a license, and the application must be filed at least 120 calendar days before.
findings.quote: The Closing shall take place on February 26, 2027, being the forty-fifth (45th) day after the Effective Date, whether or not the Department has approved the CHOW Application or issued a license to Buyer as of that date.

findings.issue: The seller's covenant is to notify the Department 30 days before the closing. The outgoing licensee must report the planned change 120 calendar days before the anticipated change and may not relinquish operations until the incoming applicant is approved.
findings.quote: Seller shall give written notice of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement to the Department not later than thirty (30) days prior to the Closing Date.

findings.issue: The interim management agreement takes effect at signing and gives the buyer's affiliate exclusive control of operations, spending, direct-care staffing and admissions before licensure. Management agreements that transfer operational control or let another entity make financial decisions or direct staffing are covered by the prior-approval requirement.
findings.quote: Commencing on the Effective Date and continuing until the Department issues a license to Buyer, Manager shall have exclusive authority to direct the day-to-day operations of the Facility, including approval of all expenditures, the hiring, scheduling and assignment of nursing and other direct-care staff, and the admission and discharge of residents.

findings.issue: The administrator and director of nursing are employees with no equity in the seller, yet must sign a two-year, 30-mile noncompete as a closing delivery. The sale-of-business exception covers only a person selling goodwill or an owner disposing of an ownership interest, so the covenant is void and unlawful to require.
findings.quote: each of the Administrator and the Director of Nursing, neither of whom holds any equity interest in Seller, shall agree not to be employed by or render services to any skilled nursing facility located within thirty (30) miles of the Facility for a period of two (2) years after the Closing Date

findings.issue: The ownership schedule identifies only holders of 25 percent or more and says smaller holders will not be named in the license application. Applicants must disclose every person with a beneficial ownership interest of 5 percent or more in the licensee or its management company.
findings.quote: This Schedule lists each Person holding, directly or indirectly, a beneficial ownership interest of twenty-five percent (25%) or more in Buyer or Manager. Holders of smaller interests are passive investors and have not been, and will not be, identified in the CHOW Application.

findings.issue: The seller must terminate every employee at closing on as little as 10 days' notice, and the buyer has no obligation to rehire. The facility has had more than 75 employees for the past 12 months, so a mass layoff or termination requires 60 days' written notice.
findings.quote: Seller shall terminate the employment of all Facility Employees effective as of 11:59 p.m. on the Closing Date and shall deliver written notice of termination to each Facility Employee not later than ten (10) days prior to the Closing Date.

findings.issue: Licensing is expressly not a closing condition, and the real property and business pass to the buyer even if its application is still pending, with the buyer operating under the seller's license. The property and business may not be transferred until the buyer qualifies for a license or provisional license.
findings.quote: If the License Application remains pending on the Closing Date, title to the Real Property and the Business shall nonetheless transfer to Buyer at the Closing, and Buyer shall operate the Community under the Existing License until Buyer's own license is issued.

findings.issue: The communications protocol has the seller notify the Department of the proposed sale seven days before closing. The licensee must give written notice to the Department at least 30 days before the transfer, or when a bona fide offer is made, whichever period is longer.
findings.quote: Seller shall deliver written notice of the proposed sale to the Department not later than seven (7) days prior to the Closing Date

findings.issue: The seller must terminate every employee as of the closing date on 14 days' notice, and the buyer has no duty to hire any of them. The community has had at least 85 employees over the prior 12 months, so a mass layoff or termination requires 60 days' written notice.
findings.quote: Seller shall terminate all Community Employees effective as of the Closing Date, and shall give each Community Employee written notice of termination at least fourteen (14) days before the Closing Date.

findings.issue: The buyer has until 45 days after the due diligence period expires, which is about 75 days after signing and after the scheduled closing, to file its license application. The buyer must apply for a license within five days of the seller's acceptance of the offer.
findings.quote: Buyer shall prepare and file with the Department a complete License Application not later than forty-five (45) days after the expiration of the Due Diligence Period.

findings.issue: The buyer waives the tax clearance certificate and agrees that nothing will be withheld from the price for the seller's sales or use tax, although the seller holds a seller's permit. A buyer who does not withhold until the seller produces a receipt or certificate becomes personally liable for the seller's unpaid tax up to the purchase price.
findings.quote: Buyer waives any requirement that Seller obtain a tax clearance certificate from the California Department of Tax and Fee Administration, and no portion of the Purchase Price shall be withheld at the Closing on account of any sales or use tax liability of Seller.

findings.issue: Written notice to each resident or legal representative is due only 10 days before the closing. On a sale that results in a new license, the licensee must give that notice at least 30 days before the transfer, or when a bona fide offer is made, whichever period is longer.
findings.quote: Seller shall deliver written notice of the sale to each resident of the Community or the resident's legal representative not later than ten (10) days prior to the Closing Date, in a form reasonably approved by Buyer.

findings.issue: The executive director and memory care program director, who are employees with no membership interest in the seller, must agree to an 18-month, 25-mile noncompete as a condition of being hired by the buyer. They are not selling goodwill or an ownership interest, so no exception applies and requiring the covenant is unlawful.
findings.quote: As a condition of any offer of employment by Buyer, the Executive Director and the Memory Care Program Director, who are employees and hold no membership interest in Seller, shall each agree that for eighteen (18) months after separation from Buyer for any reason he or she will not work for any assisted living or memory care community within twenty-five (25) miles of the Community.

findings.issue: This provision may be one-sided and should be reviewed.
findings.quote: (c) Property Seller holds fee title to the Real Property, and each Operating Seller holds good title to the assets it is selling.

findings.issue: The escrow instructions waive any tax clearance certificate or receipt and direct release of the full price to the sellers with no holdback, although both operating sellers hold seller's permits. A buyer who does not withhold until a receipt or certificate is produced becomes personally liable for the seller's unpaid sales and use tax up to the purchase price.
findings.quote: Each Buyer waives delivery of any certificate of tax clearance or receipt from the California Department of Tax and Fee Administration, and Escrow Holder is instructed to disburse the entire remaining Purchase Price to Sellers at the Closing without holdback for sales or use taxes.

findings.issue: From the signing date the buyer's advisory affiliate may veto expenditures over $5,000 and set nurse staffing ratios and direct-care staffing levels, which the seller must implement. Agreements that let another entity make financial decisions or direct direct-care staffing are covered by the prior-approval requirement, and no approval has been obtained.
findings.quote: From and after the Effective Date, Advisor shall have the right to approve or reject any expenditure of the Skilled Nursing Facility in excess of $5,000 and to set nurse staffing ratios, shift schedules and direct-care staffing levels for the Skilled Nursing Facility, and SNF Seller shall implement each such decision.

findings.issue: The admission practices the buyer must continue for 24 months require every prospective skilled nursing resident to sign a binding arbitration addendum before a bed is assigned and allow cancellation for only 10 days. A facility may not require arbitration as a condition of admission and must give a right to rescind within 30 calendar days of signing.
findings.quote: Each prospective resident of the Skilled Nursing Facility must sign the Binding Arbitration Addendum before a bed is assigned. A resident who signs may cancel the Addendum only by written notice received within ten (10) days after the date of signing.

findings.issue: The syndication clause lets any investor with less than 20 percent of the skilled nursing buyer come in without Department approval and without being named in the application. Every holder of a beneficial interest of 5 percent or more must be disclosed, and no one may acquire 5 percent or more of a licensee without the Department's prior written approval.
findings.quote: Any investor that acquires a beneficial ownership interest of less than twenty percent (20%) in SNF Buyer, whether before or after the Closing, may be admitted without the prior approval of CDPH and need not be identified in the CHOW Application or any supplement to it.

findings.issue: If approval has not come by the outside date, the seller may deliver possession and operational control of the skilled nursing facility and the buyer must close anyway. The outgoing licensee may not relinquish ownership, operations or management until the Department approves the incoming applicant.
findings.quote: If CDPH has not approved the CHOW Application by the Outside Date, SNF Seller may, at its election, deliver possession and operational control of the Skilled Nursing Facility to SNF Buyer on the Outside Date, and SNF Buyer shall accept such delivery and close the purchase of the SNF Assets, notwithstanding the absence of CDPH approval.

findings.issue: The buyer may wait until 60 calendar days before the anticipated closing date to file its application with the Department of Public Health. The application to acquire or operate a skilled nursing facility must be filed at least 120 calendar days before.
findings.quote: SNF Buyer shall file the CHOW Application with CDPH not later than sixty (60) calendar days prior to the Anticipated Closing Date.

findings.issue: The milestone schedule sets resident notice for the assisted living facility at 15 days before the closing date. On a sale resulting in a new license, each resident or legal representative must receive written notice at least 30 days before the transfer, or when a bona fide offer is made, whichever period is longer.
findings.quote: RCFE Seller shall deliver written notice of the transfer to each resident of the Assisted Living Facility, or the resident's legal representative, on or before the fifteenth (15th) day preceding the Closing Date.

findings.issue: The assisted living assets and parcel transfer at closing even if the Department of Social Services has issued no license or provisional license to the buyer. The property and business of a residential care facility for the elderly may not be transferred until the buyer qualifies for a license or provisional license.
findings.quote: The transfer of the RCFE Assets and the RCFE Parcel shall occur at the Closing concurrently with the transfer of the SNF Assets, whether or not CDSS has then issued a license or provisional license to RCFE Buyer for the Assisted Living Facility.

findings.issue: Section 6.5 conditions payment of earned, unpaid Base Salary and earned Annual Bonus (clauses (i) and (ii) of the Accrued Obligations) on the executive signing a general release. An employer may not require a release of a claim for wages due unless those wages have been paid.
findings.quote: including the Accrued Obligations described in clauses (i) and (ii) of Section 1.1(a), is conditioned on Executive signing the Release and the Release becoming effective and irrevocable within sixty (60) days after the Termination Date

findings.issue: Schedule 1, paragraph 4 makes the executive bear phone, internet and home office costs used for Company work and waive reimbursement. The employer must reimburse necessary business expenses and a waiver of that right is void.
findings.quote: Executive shall bear, without reimbursement from the Company, the cost of Executive's mobile phone service, home internet service and home office equipment and supplies used in performing services for the Company, and Executive waives any claim to be reimbursed for those costs.

findings.issue: Section 3.6 requires the executive to repay the full amount of an earned and paid Annual Bonus if the executive resigns within twelve months after payment, and allows set-off. An employer may not collect back wages already paid.
findings.quote: If Executive resigns for any reason within twelve (12) months after the date on which an Annual Bonus is paid, Executive shall repay to the Company, within thirty (30) days after the Termination Date, the full gross amount of that Annual Bonus

findings.issue: Section 9.2 bars the executive from working for any competing business in the United States for twelve months after termination. A noncompete in an employment contract is void however narrowly tailored, and it is unlawful to include one.
findings.quote: For a period of twelve (12) months after the Termination Date, Executive shall not, anywhere in the United States, be employed by, provide services to, or serve as an officer, director or consultant of any Competing Business in a finance, strategy or executive capacity.

findings.issue: Section 4.2 forfeits accrued, unused vacation when the Company terminates for Cause. An employment contract may not provide for forfeiture of vested vacation on termination; it must be paid as wages at the final rate.
findings.quote: If the Company terminates Executive's employment for Cause, all accrued and unused vacation shall be forfeited as of the Termination Date and no payment shall be made for it.

findings.issue: This provision may be one-sided and should be reviewed.
findings.quote: A. The Company designs, manufactures and sells implantable cardiac rhythm monitors, catheter-based ablation systems and related single-use accessories, and is preparing for a possible financing or public offering during the next thirty-six months.

findings.issue: Section 8.2 assigns every invention made during the Term whether or not on working hours, with Company resources or related to the Company's business, and the agreement gives no written notice of the statutory exclusion. The assignment cannot reach inventions developed entirely on the employee's own time without employer resources that are unrelated to the employer's business.
findings.quote: at any time during the Term, whether or not during working hours, whether or not with the use of the Company's equipment, facilities or information, and whether or not related to the Company's business

findings.issue: Schedule A, Part 3 requires the executive to use a personal vehicle for work travel, deems the cost included in salary and bars any claim for mileage, fuel, tolls or parking. The employer must reimburse necessary business expenses and a waiver of that right is void.
findings.quote: The Base Salary is deemed to include full payment for all costs of that use, and the Executive is not entitled to, and will not submit any claim for, mileage, fuel, tolls, parking or other vehicle costs.

findings.issue: Section 9.2 bars the executive, who is an employee and not a seller of a business, from working for or owning any senior living operator within fifty miles of a Community for eighteen months after termination. A noncompete in an employment contract is void and unlawful to include.
findings.quote: For eighteen (18) months after the Date of Termination, the Executive shall not own, manage, operate, consult for or be employed by any person that owns or operates an assisted living, memory care or independent living community located within fifty (50) miles of any Community.

findings.issue: Exhibit A, paragraph 2 makes earned, unpaid Base Salary and the earned Annual Incentive part of the consideration for the release and says the executive is not entitled to them without signing. An employer may not require a release of a claim for wages due unless those wages have been paid.
findings.quote: In exchange for the Executive's release and other promises in this Separation Agreement, the Company will pay the Executive (a) all Base Salary earned through the Separation Date that has not yet been paid, (b) any Annual Incentive earned for the Fiscal Year completed before the Separation Date that has not yet been paid

findings.issue: Section 4.3 requires the executive to pay back an amount equal to three months of Base Salary already paid if the executive resigns in the first year, labelled as recruitment cost recovery. An employer may not collect back any part of wages already paid.
findings.quote: If the Executive resigns for any reason before the first anniversary of the Start Date, the Executive shall pay the Company, as reimbursement of its recruitment costs, an amount equal to three (3) months of the Base Salary previously paid to the Executive.

findings.issue: Section 8.2 extends the assignment to developments made on the executive's own time, with the executive's own equipment, without Company information and unrelated to the business, and has the executive waive any law limiting the assignment; no written notice of the statutory exclusion is given. The assignment cannot apply to those inventions.
findings.quote: This assignment extends to Developments that the Executive creates on the Executive's own time, with the Executive's own equipment and without Proprietary Information, and that do not relate to the business of the Company Group, and the Executive waives the benefit of any law that would limit its scope.

findings.issue: Section 6.1 gives the Company thirty days after the Date of Termination to pay earned salary, earned incentive and vacation pay. Earned wages are due immediately on discharge and within 72 hours on resignation without notice.
findings.quote: The Company will pay all earned and unpaid Base Salary, Annual Incentive and vacation pay within thirty (30) days after the Date of Termination.

findings.issue: Exhibit A, paragraph 8 bars any statement about workplace conduct, including conduct believed unlawful, and paragraph 10 gives 48 hours to sign; the form never tells the executive of the right to consult an attorney. A separation agreement may not prohibit disclosure of information about unlawful acts in the workplace, and the employer must give notice of the right to consult an attorney and at least five business days.
findings.quote: The Executive shall not make any statement, to any person and by any means, about conduct in the workplaces of the Company or its Communities, including any claimed harassment, discrimination, retaliation, resident care concern or other conduct that the Executive believes was unlawful

findings.issue: Schedule 1, Part D withholds a Quarterly Bonus already earned for a completed quarter until the executive signs a general release, and denies it if she declines. An employer may not require a release of a claim for wages due unless those wages have been paid.
findings.quote: the Company will pay that earned Quarterly Bonus only after Executive has signed and delivered a general release of all claims against the Company in the form the Company provides, and no such Quarterly Bonus will be payable if Executive declines to sign the release

findings.issue: Section 13.6 requires the executive to keep her salary, bonus and equity confidential and not discuss them with any other employee. An employer may not require an employee to refrain from disclosing the amount of her wages.
findings.quote: Executive shall keep the amount of her Base Salary, Target Variable Compensation, Quarterly Bonuses and equity confidential and shall not disclose or discuss any of them with any other employee of the Company, including the members of her sales team.

findings.issue: Schedule 1, Part E makes the executive pay, without reimbursement, for a home office the position requires and for automobile travel in her territory. The employer must reimburse necessary business expenses and an agreement to waive that right is void.
findings.quote: Executive shall therefore bear, at her own cost and without reimbursement, all expenses of her home office (including internet service, mobile phone service, printing and office supplies) and all expenses of automobile travel within the Western Region, including mileage, fuel, tolls and parking.

findings.issue: Section 4.2 pays out no more than forty hours of accrued vacation at termination and forfeits the rest. An employment contract may not provide for forfeiture of vested vacation on termination; all of it is paid as wages at the final rate.
findings.quote: On the Termination Date the Company will pay Executive for not more than forty (40) hours of accrued and unused vacation, and any accrued balance above forty (40) hours will be forfeited.

findings.issue: Exhibit B, section B-5 says the covenants are governed by North Carolina law and enforceable in any court regardless of where the executive resides or where the agreement was signed, and has her agree not to argue otherwise. A contract void under the chapter is unenforceable regardless of where and when it was signed, and the employer may not try to enforce it.
findings.quote: The covenants in this Exhibit B shall be governed by North Carolina law and shall be enforceable by the Company in any court of competent jurisdiction regardless of where Executive resides or works and regardless of where this Agreement was signed or performed.

findings.issue: Exhibit B, section B-2 bars the executive from taking employment with or serving any Listed Competitor for nine months after termination. A noncompete in an employment contract is void no matter how narrowly tailored, and it is unlawful to include one.
findings.quote: During the nine (9) months that follow the Termination Date, Executive shall not accept employment with, or provide sales, sales management, consulting or advisory services to, any Listed Competitor, whether in the Western Region or elsewhere in North America.

findings.issue: Section 3.6 makes the executive give back the Quarterly Bonus already paid for the last completed quarter if she resigns on less than thirty days' notice, and lets the Company deduct it from final pay. An employer may not collect back any part of wages already paid.
findings.quote: If Executive resigns on less than thirty (30) days' written notice, Executive shall return to the Company the Quarterly Bonus paid to her for the most recently completed fiscal quarter, and the Company may deduct that amount from her final paycheck.

findings.issue: Sections 12.1 and 12.2 apply North Carolina law to all employment claims and require suit exclusively in North Carolina, with a waiver of any California forum, while the recitals state that the executive lives and works primarily in California and was not represented by counsel. An employer may not require such an employee to litigate California claims outside California or give up California law.
findings.quote: shall be governed by and construed under the laws of the State of North Carolina, without regard to any conflict of laws rule that would apply the law of another state

findings.issue: This provision may be one-sided and should be reviewed.
findings.quote: "Quota" means the New ARR target assigned to the Western Region for a fiscal quarter or fiscal year under the Incentive Plan.

findings.issue: During the consensual month-to-month holdover the landlord may raise rent by any amount on 10 days' notice. For a qualified commercial tenant on a month-to-month tenancy an increase needs at least 30 days' written notice, and 90 days if it is more than 10 percent.
findings.quote: Landlord may increase Monthly Base Rent by any amount, effective ten (10) days after written notice of the increase is delivered to Tenant

findings.issue: The lease recites that the tenant is a qualified commercial tenant, yet repair costs are charged in full even when the landlord recovers them from insurance, a warranty or a third party, with no credit. Costs reimbursed by insurance or a third party cannot be included.
findings.quote: whether or not Landlord later recovers insurance proceeds, warranty payments or reimbursement from another tenant or third party on account of the same cost, and Landlord shall not be required to credit any such recovery against Operating Costs

findings.issue: The late charge is 20 percent of the overdue amount for every month or part of a month, with no grace period, and it accrues together with default interest on the same amount. That is hard to square with a reasonable estimate of the landlord's cost of a late payment.
findings.quote: a late charge equal to twenty percent (20%) of the overdue amount for each month or part of a month that the amount remains unpaid

findings.issue: The tenant's share of operating costs is whatever the landlord assigns in its sole discretion and need not be proportionate to floor area or follow any written method. For a qualified commercial tenant the costs must be allocated proportionately by square footage or another documented method.
findings.quote: in such manner as Landlord determines in its sole discretion, which need not be proportionate to the floor area of the Premises or follow any fixed or written method

findings.issue: The lease invokes the continuation remedy of section 1951.4 but lets the landlord withhold consent to any assignment or sublease in its sole and absolute discretion. The remedy is available only if the tenant may sublet or assign subject at most to reasonable standards or consent not unreasonably withheld.
findings.quote: Landlord may grant or withhold its consent to any proposed Transfer in Landlord's sole and absolute discretion, for any reason or for no reason

findings.issue: The accessibility section allocates ADA and Title 24 compliance costs but the lease never states whether the premises have had a Certified Access Specialist inspection and has no statutory CASp notice paragraph.
findings.quote: This Shopping Center Lease (this "Lease") is dated as of January 12, 2027 (the "Effective Date") and is made between Tamsin Ridge Retail Partners, LLC, a California limited liability company ("Landlord"), and Finch & Thimble Fiber Arts, LLC, a California limited liability company ("Tenant").

findings.issue: The deposit is to be returned within 90 days after the Expiration Date. A commercial deposit must be returned no later than 30 days from the date the landlord receives possession.
findings.quote: to Tenant within ninety (90) days after the Expiration Date, together with a written statement of any amounts applied

findings.issue: The accessibility section says the landlord makes no statement on whether the premises have had a Certified Access Specialist inspection and has the tenant waive the statement and any related notice. Every commercial lease must state whether a CASp inspection has occurred and, if no certificate has been issued, include the statutory notice.
findings.quote: Landlord makes no statement in this Lease as to whether the Premises have or have not undergone inspection by a Certified Access Specialist, and Tenant waives any right to receive such a statement or any related notice from Landlord.

findings.issue: The lease invokes the section 1951.4 continuation remedy, but says that while the landlord uses it the assignment article does not apply, the tenant has no right to assign or sublet, and the landlord may refuse any transferee without regard to reasonableness. The remedy is available only if the tenant may sublet or assign subject at most to reasonable standards or consent not unreasonably withheld.
findings.quote: Article 15 shall not apply, Tenant shall have no right to assign this Lease or sublet the Premises, and Landlord may refuse any proposed assignee or subtenant without regard to whether the refusal is reasonable

findings.issue: The landlord keeps the deposit after surrender and returns it 60 days after it delivers the operating expense reconciliation for the year the term ends, which can be many months after it gets possession. The deposit must be returned no later than 30 days from the date the landlord receives possession.
findings.quote: shall return the balance to Tenant within sixty (60) days after Landlord delivers the Reconciliation Statement for the calendar year in which the Term ends

findings.issue: This provision may be one-sided and should be reviewed.
findings.quote: Section 15.6 Tenant Remains Liable. No Transfer releases Tenant. Landlord's consent to one Transfer does not waive the need for consent to another. Tenant shall pay Landlord's reasonable legal fees for reviewing a request, up to $2,500.

findings.issue: The tenant owes $2,000 for every day an estoppel certificate is late, whether or not any sale or loan is pending or delayed. A fixed daily sum with no link to likely loss may have been unreasonable when the lease was made.
findings.quote: as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, the sum of $2,000 for each day after the tenth day until the certificate is delivered

findings.issue: The parties waive jury trial in the lease itself, before any dispute exists. A jury may be waived only in the ways listed in subdivision (f), and a contract clause signed before a dispute is not one of them.
findings.quote: Landlord and Tenant each knowingly and voluntarily waive the right to a trial by jury in any action, proceeding or counterclaim brought by either of them against the other

findings.issue: Any late installment, however small, triggers an immediate charge of 15 percent of the entire monthly base rent, on top of default interest. A charge that does not vary with the amount overdue is hard to defend as a reasonable estimate of the landlord's administrative cost.
findings.quote: a late charge equal to fifteen percent (15%) of the full Monthly Base Rent then in effect, whatever the amount of the installment that is late

findings.issue: The refund is due 30 days after the later of surrender and the date the landlord finishes any move-out work the tenant left undone, so the landlord can hold the deposit well past 30 days after it has possession. The deposit must be returned no later than 30 days from the date the landlord receives possession.
findings.quote: within thirty (30) days after the later of (a) the date Lessee surrenders possession of the Premises to Lessor and (b) the date on which Lessor has completed all repair, restoration and removal work

findings.issue: The guaranty schedule has the guarantor waive a jury for any claim under the guaranty or the lease and agree to a bench trial, before any dispute exists. A jury may be waived only in the ways listed in subdivision (f), and a pre-dispute contract clause is not one of them.
findings.quote: Guarantor irrevocably waives, to the extent the law allows, any right to have a jury decide any claim, defense or counterclaim arising under this Guaranty or the Lease, and agrees that any such matter will be tried by a judge sitting without a jury.

findings.issue: The lease flatly prohibits any assignment or sublease and says the landlord need not consider a request, yet it also invokes the section 1951.4 remedy of keeping the lease in effect after abandonment. That remedy is available only if the tenant may sublet or assign subject at most to reasonable standards or consent not unreasonably withheld.
findings.quote: shall not sublet all or any part of the Premises, and shall not permit any other person or organization to occupy or share the Premises, and Lessor is not required to consider or respond to any request for consent to do so

findings.issue: The lease says the premises have not had a Certified Access Specialist inspection and then goes straight to cost allocation. Where no disability access inspection certificate has been issued, the lease must include the statutory CASp notice paragraph, and it does not.
findings.quote: The Premises have not undergone inspection by a Certified Access Specialist.

findings.issue: During the month-to-month tenancy the landlord may raise base rent by 20 percent, more than once a year, on 30 days' notice. The lease recites that the tenant is a qualified commercial tenant, so an increase of more than 10 percent over the prior 12 months needs at least 90 days' written notice.
findings.quote: Lessor may increase the Base Rent for the month-to-month tenancy by twenty percent (20%) over the Base Rent then being paid, and may do so more than once in any year, by giving Lessee thirty (30) days' written notice

findings.issue: A park rule charges $1,000 per trailer for each day or part of a day a trailer is outside its assigned stall, with no notice or chance to move it. A fixed sum of that size for a parking infraction may bear no reasonable relation to any loss the landlord could have expected when the lease was made.
findings.quote: the occupant shall pay Lessor $1,000 per trailer for each day or part of a day, as liquidated damages, which Lessor may add to the next installment of Rent without prior notice or an opportunity to move the trailer

findings.issue: The operating expense schedule lets the landlord bill any unbilled cost incurred at any time in the term or in the 36 months before it began, regardless of age. For a qualified commercial tenant the costs must have been incurred in the prior 18 months or be reasonably expected in the next 12.
findings.quote: incurred at any time during the Lease Term or during the thirty-six (36) months before the Start Date and has not previously billed to an occupant of the Premises, without regard to how long ago the cost was incurred

findings.issue: Exhibit B, item B-2 names a single manufacturer and model for the pumps and refuses all substitutions, without the words "or equal" and without reciting any finding. Specifications may not name a product by brand or trade name unless followed by "or equal", subject to exceptions that require a finding.
findings.quote: Submersible pumps shall be Vortigern Hydraulics Model VH-450 dry-pit submersible units. No substitutions will be considered, and no request to furnish an alternate manufacturer will be reviewed.

findings.issue: Section 9.4 gives Contractor 45 days to furnish certified payroll records and says no penalty applies within that period. Certified payroll records must be supplied within 10 days of a written request, with a penalty of $100 per worker per day after that.
findings.quote: Contractor shall furnish a certified copy of the payroll records to the District or the Division of Labor Standards Enforcement within forty-five (45) days after receipt of a written request, and no penalty or withholding shall apply to any request satisfied within that period.

findings.issue: Section 4.3 gives the District 60 days to pay a progress payment and bars interest on late payment. A local agency that does not pay an undisputed, properly submitted request within 30 days of receipt owes interest at the legal rate.
findings.quote: The District shall pay each approved Application for Payment within sixty (60) days after the District Engineer's receipt of the Application, and no interest, late charge or other compensation shall accrue or be payable on any progress payment made after that date.

findings.issue: Section 10.2 sets the payment bond at 50 percent of the Contract Price. On a public works contract over $25,000 the payment bond must be not less than 100 percent of the contract price.
findings.quote: a payment bond in a penal sum equal to fifty percent (50%) of the Contract Price, securing payment of all persons furnishing labor, materials, equipment or services for the Work

findings.issue: The Work includes trenches 6 to 18 feet deep and bore pits about 24 feet deep, yet Section 6.1 puts all subsurface and latent condition risk on Contractor with no price or time adjustment. A local public works contract with excavation deeper than four feet must contain the statutory differing-site-conditions clause (notice, agency investigation and change order), and this contract has none.
findings.quote: Contractor assumes all risk of subsurface and latent physical conditions at the Site, whether or not indicated in the Contract Documents or differing from those ordinarily encountered, including rock, groundwater, unsuitable soils and buried debris, and no adjustment of the Contract Price or Contract Time shall be made on account of any such condition.

findings.issue: Section 8.1 requires listing only of Subcontractors above 5 percent of the total Bid and lets Contractor use unlisted Subcontractors below that level. The prime must list each subcontractor doing work worth more than one-half of 1 percent of the prime's total bid.
findings.quote: Contractor was required to list in its Bid only those Subcontractors who will perform work or labor or render service in an amount in excess of five percent (5%) of Contractor's total Bid, and Contractor may engage any Subcontractor below that threshold without listing or notice to the District.

findings.issue: Section 4.4 withholds 10 percent of each progress payment and 10 percent of the Contract Price in total. Retention may not exceed 5 percent of a payment or 5 percent of the contract price, and the contract recites no finding that would allow more.
findings.quote: From each progress payment the District shall withhold ten percent (10%) of the amount otherwise due as retention, and the total retention held by the District shall equal ten percent (10%) of the Contract Price until Final Completion.

findings.issue: Section 9.6 states the eight-hour day and the overtime rate but the contract nowhere stipulates that Contractor forfeits $25 per worker per day for work over 8 hours a day or 40 hours a week in violation of the article. The contract must contain that stipulation.
findings.quote: Workers employed on the Work may be required or permitted to work more than eight (8) hours in any one calendar day or forty (40) hours in any one calendar week only if they are compensated for all hours in excess of those limits at not less than one and one-half (1.5) times the basic rate of pay.

findings.issue: This provision may be one-sided and should be reviewed.
findings.quote: (c) If Contractor disputes the District's response, or the District fails to respond within the time allowed, Contractor may demand in writing, by registered or certified mail, an informal meet and confer conference, which the District shall schedule within thirty (30) Days after receipt of the dema

findings.issue: Section 7.4 limits Contractor to a time extension for any delay, including delay caused by the District, and waives delay damages. A clause that limits the contractor to a time extension does not bar damages for agency-caused delay that is unreasonable and was not contemplated by the parties, and a waiver of that rule is void.
findings.quote: An extension of the Contract Time shall be Contractor's sole and exclusive remedy for any delay, disruption, interference or hindrance from any cause whatsoever, including delay caused by the District or its consultants, and Contractor waives any claim for damages, extended overhead or other compensation on account of delay.

findings.issue: Section 7.1 requires listing only of Subcontractors performing more than 3 percent of the total Bid. The prime must list each subcontractor doing work worth more than one-half of 1 percent of the prime's total bid.
findings.quote: Contractor's Bid listed, and Contractor is required to identify, only those Subcontractors performing work in an amount in excess of three percent (3%) of Contractor's total Bid.

findings.issue: This provision may be one-sided and should be reviewed.
findings.quote: (b) seismic strengthening, including new concrete shear walls at grid lines 2 and 9, steel collectors at the roof diaphragm, and new spread footings and grade beams requiring excavation to a depth of approximately seven (7) feet below the existing slab;

findings.issue: Section 9.2 waives the payment bond. A payment bond of not less than 100 percent of the contract price is required before work starts on a public works contract over $25,000.
findings.quote: In consideration of Contractor's financial strength and the retention held under Article 5, the City waives the requirement of a payment bond for this Project, and Contractor shall not be required to furnish one.

findings.issue: Section 9.5 makes Contractor indemnify City for Claims arising from City's active negligence, excepting only sole willful misconduct. A clause in a construction contract with a public agency that makes the contractor liable for the agency's active negligence is void.
findings.quote: including Claims arising from the active or passive negligence of the City or any other Indemnitee, excepting only Claims caused by the sole willful misconduct of the City

findings.issue: Section 6.6 applies the apprenticeship requirements only to Contractor and to Subcontractors with subcontracts over $500,000. The statutory exemption reaches only contracts of general contractors, or of specialty contractors not bidding through a general, that involve less than $30,000.
findings.quote: The apprenticeship requirements of Labor Code section 1777.5 shall apply only to Contractor and to Subcontractors whose subcontracts exceed Five Hundred Thousand Dollars ($500,000); all other Subcontractors are exempt from employing apprentices and from making training fund contributions.

findings.issue: Section 5.2 allows City 75 days to pay an undisputed, properly submitted Payment Request and says amounts paid in that period bear no interest. A local agency that does not pay within 30 days of receipt owes interest at the legal rate.
findings.quote: Payment of each undisputed progress payment shall be made within seventy-five (75) days after the City's receipt of a properly submitted Payment Request. Amounts paid within that period shall not bear interest.

findings.issue: Section 11.4 holds retention for 120 days after completion and bars any interest or charge. Retention must be released within 60 days after completion, and late payment carries a charge of 2 percent per month.
findings.quote: The City shall release the retention, less amounts withheld under this Contract, one hundred twenty (120) days after the date of completion of the Work, and no interest or charge shall accrue on retention held during that period.

findings.issue: Section 6.2 says prevailing wage law does not apply to demolition, site clearing, landscaping and final cleaning labor and lets Contractor set those wage rates. Prevailing wages must be paid to workers on a public work over $1,000, and this is an $8,415,000 public project.
findings.quote: Labor for demolition, site clearing, landscaping and final cleaning is not subject to prevailing wage law, and Contractor may set the wage rates for those classifications at its discretion.

findings.issue: Section 9.06 covers the eight-hour day, time records and overtime pay, but the contract contains no stipulation that Contractor forfeits $25 per worker per day for work over 8 hours a day or 40 hours a week in violation of the article. The contract must contain that stipulation.
findings.quote: Workers may be employed for more than eight (8) hours per day or forty (40) hours per week upon compensation for all excess hours at not less than one and one-half times the basic rate of pay.

findings.issue: Section 3.06 denies any damages for delay even when the District caused it and the delay was unreasonable and not contemplated, limits Contractor to a time extension, and waives any contrary statute. Such a clause does not bar damages for agency-caused, unreasonable, uncontemplated delay, and a waiver of that rule is void.
findings.quote: Contractor shall not be entitled to any damages or additional compensation for delay, whether or not caused by the District, unreasonable in duration or within the contemplation of the parties at the time of contracting; Contractor's only relief for delay is an extension of the Contract Time, and Contractor waives the benefit of any statute to the contrary.

findings.issue: Section 9.04 gives Contractor 30 days to furnish certified payroll records and defers penalties until the sixtieth day. Certified payroll records must be supplied within 10 days of a written request, and the penalty of $100 per worker per day runs after that.
findings.quote: Contractor shall furnish certified copies of payroll records to the District or to the Division of Labor Standards Enforcement within thirty (30) days after receipt of a written request; the penalties of this Section shall not begin to accrue until the sixtieth (60th) day after the request.

findings.issue: Section 5.03 retains 7.5 percent of each progress payment and up to 7.5 percent of the Contract Price. Retention may not exceed 5 percent of a payment or 5 percent of the contract price, and no finding allowing more is recited.
findings.quote: The District shall retain seven and one-half percent (7.5%) of each progress payment, and aggregate retention may reach but shall not exceed seven and one-half percent (7.5%) of the Contract Price.

findings.issue: Section 5.07 releases retention 90 days after completion and without interest. Retention must be released within 60 days after completion, and late payment carries a charge of 2 percent per month.
findings.quote: The District shall release the retention ninety (90) days after the date of completion of the Work, without interest.

findings.issue: Exhibit E, item E-2(a) names one manufacturer and model for the lifts and refuses any substitute, without the words "or equal" and without reciting any finding. Specifications may not name a product by brand or trade name unless followed by "or equal", subject to exceptions that require a finding.
findings.quote: Heavy-duty in-ground vehicle lifts shall be Grayling Liftworks Model GL-3X three-post modular lifts. The District will accept no substitute product or manufacturer for the lifts.

findings.issue: Section 11.01 extends Contractor's indemnity, regardless of fault, to Claims arising from the active negligence of the District. A clause in a construction contract with a public agency that makes the contractor liable for the agency's active negligence is void.
findings.quote: Contractor's obligations under this Section apply regardless of fault and extend to Claims arising from the active negligence of the District, its directors, officers, employees or agents.

findings.issue: Section 9.03 says Subcontractors and equipment installers with work valued under $100,000 need not register with the Department of Industrial Relations. No subcontractor may work on a public work unless registered, and the only size exemption is for projects of $25,000 or less ($15,000 or less for maintenance).
findings.quote: Subcontractors and equipment installers whose work on the Project is valued at less than One Hundred Thousand Dollars ($100,000) are not required to be registered with the Department of Industrial Relations.
